📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Privacy and cybersecurity have become an important part of the internet browsing experience in the current world. VPNs, or Virtual Private Networks, have grown in usage and in relevance over the years due to this.

In a recent development, however, not all VPNs offer the same level of performance, transparency, value, or protection as others; some are great for advanced privacy features, while others are better for streaming. Here is our list of the top picks for the month:.

It has been revealed that expressVPN aims to make online privacy secure and internet access straightforward for everyone. It is available on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. Lightway is a proprietary VPN protocol designed to establish connections swiftly and reduce battery consumption while also improving reliability when switching between networks.

There are 3 subscription tiers on ExpressVPN: Basic, which has the core VPN protection and encrypted connections, along with essential privacy tools. Advanced, with additional security features and expanded protection tools, and password management options—lastly, Pro, a comprehensive package with additional privacy and identity-protection features.

CyberGhost VPN focuses on accessible internet privacy and user-friendly VPN applications. The platform allows for various subscription looks for owners, and long-term plans have lower monthly pricing. It has specialised server categories that let users select servers that are optimized for streaming, downloading, and general browsing.

Recent findings suggest that the platform also has a no-logs policy, security features like AES-256 encryption, an automatic kill switch, split tunnelling, and DNS leak protection. CyberGhost is a great option for beginner-level users who want an easy-to-use app with specialized server choices.

Sources indicate that nord VPN is one of the most popular options on the market; it has grown over the years from a conventional VPN provider into a broader cybersecurity platform. It has 3 subscription plans: Basic, Plus, and Complete. The Basic strategy has core VPN protection options and access to its server network. The Plus plan has features like password management and threat protection, while the Complete plan has VPN protection with additional security and encrypted cloud-storage services.

Industry observers note that nordLynx is a WireGuard-based VPN protocol that has been designed to deliver faster connections without having to compromise on privacy. There are also Double VPN, Onion Over VPN, split tunnelling, and an automatic kill switch.

Industry observers note that surfshark offers unlimited simultaneous device connections and has WireGuard, OpenVPN, AES-256 encryption, a kill switch, and MultiHop connections. There is an option to generate an alternative online identity and email address for users who do not want to share their details.

It has subscription plans with varying rates and features. This includes the Starter proposal with core VPN access with access to 4500 servers, ad blockers, split tunnelling and alternative ID generators. The One plan adds antivirus protection and data leak monitoring along with private search and scam protection tools to everything in the Starter plan. Lastly, the One+ plan has everything in the One plan and Incogni personal data removal from data brokers and identity theft coverage of up to $1 million.

In a recent development, proton VPN keeps user information safe without slowing them down or selling them out. It lets owners browse, stream, and connect on the internet easily while shielding their personal information and staying safe from online threats. It uses AES-256 and ChaCha20 encryption across various protocols and blocks ads, trackers and malware on paid looks.

There are various subscription plans including a free, VPN Plus and a Proton Unlimited one. Proton VPN also supports WireGuard,   , Stealth and a kill switch. On the paid plans it blocks ads, trackers and malware along with support for split tunnelling.

Private Internet Access emphasizes privacy and security while encrypting user internet traffic and masking their real IP address. It has a strict no-logs policy and supports WireGuard, OpenVPN, AES-256 encryption, split Tunnelling and a kill switch.

The MACE feature on PIA also helps to block ads, trackers and other malicious domains. Automation rules, port forwarding and encryption settings can all be customised by users on the platform.

Windscribe intends to make privacy accessible and internet freedom a reality for everyone around the world. It has a network spanning across 69 countries and 135 cities and R.O.B.E.R.T blocks ads, trackers, malware domains and any other unwanted internet destinations.

Sources indicate that the platform also has a firewall-style connection protection feature, along with a free, pro and build a initiative options. It also supports WireGuard, OpenVPN and offers static and residential IP options as well.

VPNs, as mentioned earlier, are an inseparable part of the internet experience in 2026. There are a lot of options in the market, catering to various requirements. Consumers can pick the free or the paid ones depending on the level of privacy and security they require. However, whichever VPN they choose, it is important to do their own thorough research.

Shiba Inu's exchange activity keeps on bringing more to the table. This time, 372.39 billion tokens flowed into exchanges. Inflows recorded an increase of 0.36% over 24 hours, which once again raises the chances of a surge in market pressure, data from CryptoQuant suggests.

Recent findings suggest that while the inflow number to exchanges is quite high, the total netflow doesn't hit the value of 100 billion, suggesting that the amount of inflows after withdrawals doesn't really disrupt the overall picture for Shiba Inu. That bounce looks speculative after the sell-off. Some of the buying volume may have come from orders placed prior to the drop. SHIB was up about 8.3% from the low and was still below $0.000004.

In a recent development, momentum stays as weak as before. An RSI around 27 suggests the market is still oversold, which means there are no guarantees for a quick reversal. Luckily, though, there's some bullish traction as Shiba Inu is printing the second green candle in a row, making a retrace somewhat of a possibility sooner than we might've expected.

Major-time speed performance makes Solana edge the apex crypto asset, but both are in losing key thresholds.

Solana is showing relative strength against Bitcoin while traders monitor a key level that could support a short-term bottom, according to recent analysis from More Crypto Online and Crypto Tony.

More Crypto Online highlighted that Solana (SOL) is starting to outperform Bitcoin (BTC) on the 4-hour and daily Solana price charts.

The pair has been working through a corrective structure, with price recently holding above main support zones near the 78.6% and 88.7% Fibonacci retracements on the higher timeframes.

$SOL Starts to Outperform Bitcoin pic.twitter.com/qQ8Lgrfmgr.

On the shorter-term chart, SOL is attempting to stabilize after a sharp decline, with analysts watching for a potential wave completion that could open room for a bounce if local support holds.

Sources indicate that crypto Tony noted that a short-term bottom case can be made for SOL if price reclaims a marked level on the 4-hour chart. At the time of the enhancement, SOL was trading near $74.

The analyst indicated that a reclaim of the horizontal level around the recent swing area would improve the structure, though no upcoming entries were recommended until confirmation.

Industry observers note that $SOL – Patch A case for a short term bottom can be made if we can reclaim that level marked out. No new entry for now though. pic.twitter.com/revlkbsA1s.

The chart shows a potential path higher if that level is taken back, with local resistance sitting overhead near $78–82.

As of November 20, 2026, Solana (SOL) was trading just below the $70 range after dropping furhter from the mid-$80s recorded earlier in the month.

Recent findings suggest that the popular digital asset has underperformed over the past 30 days but is now displaying early relative strength against Bitcoin on lower time-frames. Broader market conditions remain cautious, with Bitcoin itself consolidating after recent lows.

Outperformance versus Bitcoin is an early signal, but sustained strength requires SOL to hold its local lows and reclaim the identified level.

Recent findings suggest that an unfortunate try to reclaim that zone would keep the short-term structure corrective. Traders are watching the interaction between the SOL/USD support and the SOL/BTC relative chart for confirmation that the recovery attempt is gaining traction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that charles Hoskinson, founder of Cardano (ADA), has tried to clear the air regarding the utility of the cryptocurrency. This comes as ADA has fallen more than 95% from its all-time high.

Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson responded to frustrated Cardano community members who are disappointed by the blockchain’s pace of development and inability to rebound from the current slump.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 21, Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson took to X to counter criticism about the current state of Cardano.

The exchange was triggered by a joke made by an X user stating that Grand Theft Auto 6 came out before a working Cardano blockchain.

Hoskinson replied to the comment, saying: “Cardano works.”.

Later, Hoskinson addressed the poor price performance of the cryptocurrency and explained that price doesn’t always reflect the capabilities of blockchain networks.

Recent findings suggest that “Yeah. Price doesn't equal utility. Is Solana 75 percent less capable than it's all time high? It's an infinitely better product today for many more people. And so it is for Cardano,” he stated.

What this means is that even if the value of a blockchain network's native cryptocurrency is dropping, the technology can still advance.

An X user, however, contested his comparison with Solana, stating that Cardano hasn’t been able to retake its previous all-time high even after years of development.

This drew an increasingly irritated response from Hoskinson.

According to recent reports, “So every single thing a f****** scam? Everything they do failed? I’m so tired of you people,” mentioned the Cardano founder.

This recent statement by Hoskinson comes as Cardano (ADA) remains one of the worst-performing major cryptocurrencies in the current market downturn.

As per CoinGlass data, ADA is right now trading at around $0.14. The cryptocurrency is down by about 57% since the beginning of 2026.

It has lost a whopping 95.4% of its value from its all-time high of $3.09, set in September 2021.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Coinbase wants a piece of the prediction markets action, with the exchange reportedly planning a launch next year.

Right now, they don’t run their own; they borrow them. Users trade event contracts on the exchange through a Kalshi partnership. That could change next year though.

Citing sources close to the matter, a Bloomberg report claimed that Coinbase wants to roll out its own event contracts in the U.S in H1 2027. It would be open to both retail and institutional traders.

But why bother? For starters, Coinbase gets to decide what rolls out and when. Next, it keeps a bigger share of the trading fees.

There’s real money at stake here. In Q3 2026, Coinbase’s prediction markets business was already on track to bring in over $200 million a year. If you think about it, this isn’t an overnight decision. In the run up to it all, Coinbase revealed that it was buying prediction market startup The Clearing Tech giant in December 2025.

Then, in September this year, the CFTC gave the green light for its own clearing house.

All that being said, nothing’s set in stone. However, the pieces are clearly falling into place.

Crypto trading may have slowed down, but prediction markets have kept themselves out of the bleeding.

According to recent reports, since launch, revenue from the business has grown by 82% QoQ on average. In Q3 alone, daily traders went up by over 60%, compared to the quarter before.

Industry observers note that CFO Alesia Haas summed up the appeal pretty neatly. She stated,.

Prediction markets are adding another revenue stream and are less correlated to crypto volatility….

A big deal for an exchange that lives and dies by market cycles.

On the earnings call, Haas also said that the upcoming clearing house would let Coinbase run its own contracts and earn more from them.

Worth pointing out, however, that Kalshi isn’t being cut out as partner contracts will stay on the platform.

Ripple’s exposure to the XRP-only Evernorth corporate treasury since the NASDAQ debut has been an open debate. Since the October merger, Evernorth’s holdings have imposed a limitation on voting rights ownership, specifically capped at 9.99%.

This gives Ripple Lab’s executives the ability to retain economies of scale through a separate subsidiary class. That implies a strong distinction between financial exposure and voting control. The restriction doesn’t mean Ripple surrendered their additional economic exposure.

Actually, the equity interests exceeding the permitted share allocation remained in the Pathfinder units, which carry distinct rights from ordinary publicly-traded Evernorth(XRPN) shares. The complexity behind Evernorth’s $1 billion corporate treasury fund is laid out in a SEC filing.

SEC FILING: Evernorth files a prospectus supplement to register the resale of up to 73.7M Class A shares and 239,653 sponsor warrants.The firm will not receive proceeds from the resale, except on exercise of the sponsor warrants.Last reported price (Nov 16): $7.45 per… https://t.co/wXcQPJQwS5 pic.twitter.com/FakZLekF9s.

The company also had cash from its SPAC combination and later financing like convertible notes & practical warrant exercises.

Other Evernorth fund investors received miscellaneous ownership arrangements. SBI-affiliated investors were subject to a 39.9% ownership threshold, while the sponsor’s allocation reflected a 19.9% XRPN voting threshold. Evernorth’s XRPN debuted on NASDAQ on October 12, 2026.

#133115. Best Hyperliquid trading bots: AI agents and bots compared

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (923 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ambcrypto ↗ Open Full Page

Best Hyperliquid trading bots: AI agents and bots compared

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (923 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it.
  • Most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet.
  • Many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyperliquid has become one of the busiest venues for crypto perpetual futures, and a long list of tools now automate trading on it. They differ less in what they promise than in two practical questions: who decides the trades, and what the tool is allowed to do with your account. This guide compares the main Hyperliquid trading bots and AI trading agents in 2026, plus Hyperliquid’s vaults, against those questions. Each tool was compared on who decides the trades, what its key can do with your account, and what evidence of performance exists, using each provider’s own documentation in October 2026.

Most Hyperliquid tools connect through an API wallet, which Hyperliquid also calls an agent wallet. The account owner approves a separate key that can sign orders for the account but cannot withdraw or transfer funds. These approvals expire, and approving a latest wallet under the same name replaces the old one. Some tools also recommend a sub-account, which keeps the bot’s balances and positions separate. The assets stay in the user’s own Hyperliquid account throughout, which is why most Hyperliquid bots can fairly be called non-custodial.

Many tools charge through a builder fee, a small fee added to each filled order. It applies only after the user approves a maximum fee from the main wallet, and Hyperliquid caps it at 0.1% on perpetuals.

Tools are grouped by who supplies the trading logic: a managed model first, then signal execution, rule-based bots and open-source software (3Commas sits with the rule-based bots). Vaults come last because they replace a bot rather than run one. Hyperliquid’s own trading and funding fees apply to every option.

Industry observers note that alphaNet is built for Hyperliquid and supplies the trading logic itself. Consumers pick one of its deep learning strategies for crypto perpetual futures and an allocation, and the model decides when to enter and exit each trade. It connects the way the exchange intends: the user approves an agent wallet that can place and cancel orders but cannot withdraw or transfer, and trades run from the user’s own account. New deployments allow leverage up to 3× account equity. On cost, AlphaNet’s Hyperliquid trading bot charges no platform fee during the current promotional period, compared with builder fees of 0.035–0.1% per fill on several bots below; Hyperliquid’s protocol fees still apply, and a dynamic trading fee applies afterwards.

According to recent reports, A newer group of AI agent projects on Hyperliquid connect language models to an API wallet and let them place trades. They are mostly early. In the first season of Alpha Arena, a short real-money competition on Hyperliquid, four of the six language models that took part finished with losses and two with gains.

WunderTrading is built for traders whose strategy already exists as TradingView alerts or external signals. It turns those alerts into Hyperliquid orders and also offers DCA and grid bots, charging a 0.035% builder fee with no separate subscription.

goodcryptoX is a no-code app for grid, DCA, trailing, and TradingView bots on iOS, Android, and the web. Gainium covers similar bot types and adds backtesting and paper trading, with a choice between a free mode that adds a builder fee and paid aims that do not. Bitsgap brings its hosted grid and DCA bots to Hyperliquid alongside the centralised exchanges it already supports, and 3Commas, one of the most widely used bot platforms, lists Hyperliquid among its supported exchanges for spot and futures. With all of them, the bot executes your logic; the tool does not supply a trading edge.

Sources indicate that hummingbot has Hyperliquid spot and perpetual connectors and includes market-making scripts and arbitrage, TWAP, and grid executors. The self-run client charges no builder fee. It accepts either an API wallet or the main wallet’s private key; the second gives the software full control of the account, so the API wallet is the safer choice.

Rule-based bots have no platform-level record, because results depend on each user’s settings. Vaults are the most transparent option: every vault’s history is on-chain and visible in Hyperliquid’s app. Managed strategy platforms sit in between. AlphaNet publishes a running record of each strategy since its start date, and because trades run from customers’ own accounts, each user’s fills are on-chain and can be checked against it.

Instead of connecting a tool to your own account, you deposit into a vault that a leader trades. The protocol’s own vault, HLP, provides liquidity, performs liquidations, and earns a share of fees. User-run vaults follow individual strategies. Leaders take 10% of profits and must keep at least 5% of the vault, and deposits are locked for one day (four days for HLP).

The choice comes down to the two questions this guide started with. First, decide who you want making the trades: your own rules, a signal you already trust, a trained model, or a vault leader. Then check what the tool is allowed to do with your account. On Hyperliquid, most tools need only an agent wallet that can trade but not withdraw, so there is rarely a reason to hand over a main wallet key or move funds into someone else’s control.

Industry observers note that two further checks are worth making before committing real capital. The first is cost per fill: builder fees on top of Hyperliquid’s own fees can add up. The second is the record: a vault’s history is on-chain, a managed strategy should publish a live one, and a rule-based bot has none until you build your own.

Blockstream CEO Adam Back has explained the overnight sell-off on Kraken's Canadian-dollar markets that sent the exchange's BTC/CAD pair to C$24,250, or roughly $17,000, on Saturday morning, and said that the drop started with the exchange's local USD/CAD market maker.

The Blockstream CEO addressed the issue on X on Saturday in a reply to a post that tracked large sell orders hitting Kraken's BTC/CAD order book at regular intervals throughout the night.

The $17,000 figure is based on the Bank of Canada's Friday rate of C$1.4325 per U.S. dollar. Kraken's BTC/CAD pair printed the C$24,250 low on Saturday morning, according to TradingView data.

"No, the reason was USDCAD Kraken local spot FX market-maker ran out of money, as it has depegged away from market rate 1.434," Back replied.

In the same post, the Blockstream CEO mentioned that it was "more accurate to say you could buy CAD discounted.".

Later, another X user argued that the Canadian dollar was in fact overvalued on Kraken during the sell-off, since anyone who held CAD could buy anything at a discount. Back agreed with the correction.

In a recent development, "You are right. BTCUSD normal price, USDCAD CAD mispriced, like a shortage of CAD bid the price up," Back wrote.

On Sunday, the Blockstream CEO described the whole chain of events in two more posts on X.

According to Back, if the USD/CAD market maker failed, there were few buyers of BTC in Canadian dollars, and so the BTC/CAD price fell. In his view, traders would normally close such a gap with an arbitrage trade "by selling USD to CAD to buy if it BTCCAD doesn't track BTCUSD.".

Back wrote that the drop "liquidated people" and triggered stop losses "based on a local false price.".

"And then USDCAD followed because you could buy BTC cheaply in CAD, so it became logical to buy CAD way over par to take that arb," he added.

The BTC/CAD pair recovered later on Saturday, and on Sunday, it traded at C$86,236 on Kraken, according to TradingView.

Kraken stated in a statement that its Canadian-dollar trading pairs faced heavy selling pressure starting around 20:00 UTC on Friday, and prices on these pairs fell significantly below those on other markets.

The Kraken sell-off started on the same day that Bitcoin dropped to $59,370, its lowest level since July 2, according to CoinGlass data. On Friday, CoinGlass also recorded $1.57 billion in liquidations across the crypto market over 24 hours, and long positions accounted for $1.43 billion of that amount.

Still, the exchange said that every order was processed correctly and that its security teams found no evidence of a breach or compromised accounts.

"Executed trades stand," Kraken said.

Solana’s core developer, Anza, has unveiled its 2027 roadmap.

Industry observers note that structurally, the roadmap focuses on making Solana faster, more efficient, and capable of handling more activity. The network aims to double its compute capacity and cut the compute units needed for token account transactions by 80%.

It also plans to increase the number of accounts supported in each transaction from 64 to 96 and make it easier to run models fully on-chain.

Sources indicate that naturally, the question becomes whether Solana is preparing for its next growth phase. Interestingly, the previous major network upgrade was also performed by Anza.

This upgrade, called Alpenglow, brought down Solana’s finality time to 150ms from 12.8 seconds, making the network significantly faster.

Recent findings suggest that the result? As the chart above shows, Solana processed over 10 billion transactions in October, keeping monthly activity above that level. However, more than halfway through November, the network has recorded just over 2 billion transactions.

That’s 5x lower than October’s total, suggesting that the recent spike in activity may be losing steam. Given this, it might be too early to expect any bull run in 2027.

In fact, SOL is at the moment down 20% in October, which indicates that the market hasn’t seen increased demand from improving fundamentals just yet.

So, what does it say about the recent “Anthropic-driven” momentum on Solana [SOL]?

SPCX was first to demonstrate how major IPOs can bring fresh trading activity to Solana.

The launch of SpaceX’s tokenized stock, SPCX, on Solana on the 12th of June brought significant activity to the network.

The token recorded $108 million in 24-hour on-chain trading volume shortly after launch and crossed 10,000 holders within six days, with cumulative trading volume exceeding $350 million.

Notably, a similar trend has emerged following the ANT IPO launch. As the chart below reveals, Anthropic’s ANT has generated over $29 million in trading volume on Solana since launch across three issuers. Backpack’s token alone accounted for $26.8 million, or nearly 92% of the total.

This reveals how major IPO releases are bringing fresh trading activity to Solana.

Adding to this, DeFiLlama data demonstrates that Solana’s stablecoin market cap has risen nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, pointing to a fresh liquidity inflow after months of weakness.

However, the bigger picture remains mixed.

Despite the rise in on-chain activity and liquidity, SOL is still trading around $70. This suggests that the recent activity has yet to translate into stronger buying pressure.

For Solana’s 2027 roadmap to support a longer-term recovery, the network will therefore need to sustain this growth beyond short-term activity.

Anza’s 2027 roadmap aims to improve Solana’s speed, capacity, and overall network efficiency.

SPCX and ANT have boosted on-chain trading activity, but SOL’s price weakness suggests that stronger demand is still missing.

When the researchers gave each reviewer equal weight, Claude’s average accuracy was 49.1%. The test highlighted that an unsigned report can give its writer away. Estimating how often that happens across confidential peer review would take a larger, more varied sample.

The paper reports 39.3% accuracy for a subset containing 789 reviews that Pangram 4.1, an AI-text detector, had labeled human or mixed. The paper’s abstract cites that filtered rate, rounded to 39%.

Accuracy was higher on public reviews whose writers cited their own work. Claude recorded 80.2% accuracy in the group of 106 reviews with self-citations and 17.1% in the group of 1,453 without them.

Recent findings suggest that claude made mistakes even in the group where it performed best. An editor or author presented with a name from Claude would still need independent evidence to establish who wrote an unsigned review. In the final stretch of 2026, some XRP Ledger protocol features await mainnet activation, with validator support and amendment voting as the final steps to bring fresh functionality to the XRPL network.

In a recent development, in light of this, three amendments are racing against the 2026 calendar, with only a few votes left to reach a majority and enter the two-week activation period. These include SingleAssetVault, LendingProtocol and confidential transfers.

All three remain below the required validator approval threshold of over 80% support, making the final weeks of the year increasingly important for their activation prospects.

With about five weeks left in 2026, activation remains possible this year, but additional validator support for each amendment must arrive soon enough and be sustained to complete the required two-week activation window.

Recent findings suggest that the lending protocol allows on-chain fixed-term, uncollateralized loans from pooled funds in a Single Asset Vault. There are two amendments: LendingProtocolV1_1 and the original Lending Protocol amendment.

Sources indicate that the focus is on LendingProtocolV1_1, which extends the Lending Protocol and SingleAssetVault amendments with a latest closed-ended vault and cash-basis accounting. With the amendment, new loan brokers can only be created against closed-ended vaults.

LendingProtocolV1_1 has reached 70.59% support with 24 out of 34 validators voting yes, according to XRPScan data. It needs 28 votes to reach a majority, or more than 80% of 34 votes, meaning it has just four votes left.

Recent findings suggest that A major privacy amendment for the XRP Ledger, confidential transfers, has 64.71% support and 22 of 34 validators voting yes. Confidential transfers, which rely on advanced cryptography (EC-ElGamal and ZKPs), offer institutional-grade privacy for Multi-Purpose Tokens (MPTs) and need six more yes votes to enter the activation window.

SingleAssetVault creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. It has gained 73.53% support so far with 25 out of 34 validators voting in favor. Reaching more than 80% of 34 votes requires 28 votes; thus, three votes remain for it to enter the activation window.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • That’s what Elon Musk said about the idea to merge Tesla and SpaceX, back in October 2026.
  • Sources indicate that since then, however, it would seem that this somewhat fanciful idea has only accelerated.
  • It has been revealed that will it go through?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes.”.

That’s what Elon Musk said about the idea to merge Tesla and SpaceX, back in October 2026.

Sources indicate that since then, however, it would seem that this somewhat fanciful idea has only accelerated. Over the last few weeks alone, both Tesla and SpaceX have constituted special exploratory committees consisting of independent directors.

It has been revealed that will it go through? Probably, yes. After all, despite the CEO of SpaceX and Tesla claiming that he is a “conflicted party,” his companies’ shareholders have often acceded to his wishes. That’s an opinion Walter Isaacson, author of “Elon Musk,” shares too.

Especially after the entrepreneur made his case by stating,.

…there’s a lot of merit to combining the companies as we are pretty much in the Super Intelligence singularity.

Needless to say, such a merger will have some legal, regulatory, and financial implications. But what about the crypto sector?

In a recent development, tesla, Inc., the automotive and clean energy company, holds 11,509 BTC valued at over $747 million right now. Similarly, SpaceX, the aerospace manufacturer, holds 18,712 BTC worth over $1.22 billion.

In simple terms, the merger will simply be a transaction that pools in digital assets owned by both these entities into a single balance sheet. This consolidation would allow the merged entity to hold 30,221 BTC in reserves.

Those are significant numbers. However, here’s where it’s also worth looking at the context and scale and the bigger picture.

Neither Tesla nor SpaceX are crypto companies. They are primarily tech manufacturing companies with valuations of $1.54 trillion and $1.89 trillion, respectively.

Yes, they have crypto holdings, but they aren’t significant enough for each individual entity to suggest that these are more than a passing interest and a diversification opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that to put it in financial terms, for both Tesla and SpaceX, Bitcoin is a non-core balance sheet asset. For them, their BTC holdings are financially immaterial to their core CapEx. As Dr. Andrei Belonogov, Managing Partner at TechAccountingPro pointed out,.

The size of treasuries is relatively small compared to the organization’s debt maturities and non-cancellable commitments.

This will remain the case if the merger does go through. If and when it happens, the merged companies’ valuation would dwarf the value of its crypto holdings.

According to recent reports, what about after, though? This is an vital question because more often than not, non-core balance sheet assets go through a period of evaluation and restructuring and sometimes, disposal too to streamline operations and facilitate profitability.

Could this happen to the aforementioned Bitcoin holdings then? Well, that’s always a possibility. However, recent history suggests the odds are low.

Consider the purchase and sale history of both these companies, for instance. The last time Tesla sold any of its Bitcoin holdings was back in 2022. Since then, it has bought additional BTC while also holding on to the stash it already had.

Recent findings suggest that similarly, SpaceX last sold any of its holdings back in 2024. In the two years since, the aerospace manufacturer has only bought Bitcoin. Specifically, over 10K BTC in May 2026.

Now, it’s up for debate how much input the “conflicted party,” Musk, had in any of these sales or purchases. However, it is safe to assume that, given the consistencies between the two boardrooms so far, that will remain the case after the merger too.

Recent findings suggest that what about later though? Well, MetaWin COO Rory Cartwright told AMBCrypto,.

Industry observers note that the merger doesn’t necessarily mean a sell-off or any spike in price. What it will do, however, is put a roughly $2bn position into a single firm’s balance sheet. Bitcoin can be especially volatile, so that may make some investors seasick.

Will the merged entity enjoy the same degree of flexibility Tesla and SpaceX enjoyed individually when it comes to crypto sales and purchases though? According to Kevin Constantine, Senior Associate at Caldwell Law,.

Protections could become relevant to cryptocurrency holdings, particularly if management’s ability to purchase, liquidate, or transfer Bitcoin raised concerns about the companies’ valuations or the treatment of shareholders.

In a recent development, the fact that both Tesla and SpaceX refused to sell their Bitcoin in 2026, a year that has been particularly bearish for the crypto-sector, is testament to the confidence they have in this asset. It is also a sign of institutional conviction.

Recent findings suggest that after the merger, the merged entity will have the potential to be the sixth-largest corporate Bitcoin holder in the world. Only behind crypto-native firms or treasury-focused players like MicroStrategy and Metaplanet. All while Bitcoin remains its non-core balance sheet asset.

According to recent reports, that, more than anything, will be confirmation of Bitcoin’s value as a corporate treasury asset. That might not sound like much on paper, but that is still VERY bullish news.

Ripple’s dollar-pegged stablecoin, Ripple USD (RLUSD), has now entered the top five stablecoins by market cap, reaching a new all-time high in its circulating supply, a major milestone for the stablecoin less than two years after its launch. RLUSD went live in December 2024.

RLUSD has surpassed World Liberty Financial USD (USD1), Global Dollar (USDG) and PayPal USD (PYUSD) to become the fifth-largest stablecoin in the world, according to data from CoinMarketCap. Only Tether’s USDT, Circle’s USDC, Ethena’s USDe, and Dai (DAI) are ahead of it.

The milestone is proof of the rapid growth RLUSD has experienced in a competitive stablecoin market dominated by established players like Tether’s USDT and Circle’s USDC.

RLUSD’s total circulating supply across the XRP Ledger and Ethereum has reached a new high, with $2.85 billion in circulation, according to Ripple’s stablecoin tracker.

Ethereum commands $2.089 billion of this total figure, while $768 million in supply sits on the XRP Ledger. While Ethereum currently holds the larger share of RLUSD’s supply, XRPL has seen significant activity in RLUSD settlement volumes.

In March 2025, during a Bloomberg TV interview, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse projected that RLUSD would enter the top five stablecoins; that projection has now been fulfilled.

According to RWA Foundation, Ripple led weekly stablecoin growth, adding $75.4 million in the last seven days. This growth was reflected in RLUSD's market cap, allowing it to surpass World Liberty Financial USD to clinch the fifth spot in global stablecoin rankings.

Former Ripple executive Anthony Welfare highlighted this growth in a recent X post, saying, “RLUSD is the only major stablecoin growing right now.”.

Welfare noted that RLUSD supply is up nearly 20% in three weeks, rising from $2.42 billion to $2.9 billion, while USDT has fallen by $5 billion and USDC by $3 billion over the same period.

The XRP Ledger accounts for the majority of RLUSD settlements: in an analogy on X, Welfare noted that XRPL holds about 27% of RLUSD’s supply but processed 57% of its volume last week, amounting to $6.7 billion versus Ethereum, which recorded $5 billion.

Quantum Upgrade Could Be 'Particularly Challenging' for Blockchains: IOSCO

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Decrypt

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.
  • Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) noted in a report published on Thursday.
  • "Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Financial markets, including crypto, need to start preparing now for quantum computers capable of breaking the cryptography that secures them, according to the world's main forum for securities regulators.

Sources indicate that A "sufficiently capable" quantum computer could undermine widely used public-key cryptography that supports critical functions across financial markets, the International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) noted in a report published on Thursday. The cyber readiness challenge posed by quantum computing "is immediate and requires action," it said.

"Practical quantum computers capable of compromising widely used cryptography do not yet exist, but the scale and duration of the transition mean the financial sector should start preparing today," IOSCO Board Chair Jean-Paul Servais mentioned in a statement.

Industry observers note that the 63-page report cited conservative estimates that such machines could emerge between 2030 and 2035. Several industry participants consulted by IOSCO went further, arguing that firms should prepare for the possibility that they arrive within five years, potentially accelerated by AI.

According to recent reports, IOSCO remarked the migration may be particularly challenging for blockchains, because cryptography is embedded in their core architecture and any change requires coordinated action across decentralized networks. Public blockchains such as Ethereum, Solana and Tron rely heavily on elliptic curve cryptography to verify identities and validate transactions, and a powerful enough quantum computer could derive private keys from exposed public keys, a scenario known as "Q-Day.".

Industry observers note that swapping in quantum-resistant signatures comes at a cost. Signatures under ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum standard from the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, are about 2,420 bytes, roughly 35 to 40 times larger than today's 64-byte elliptic curve signatures, the report said. It cited evidence from a quantum-resistant Solana testnet that saw throughput fall by about 90% when post-quantum signatures replaced existing ones.

Recent findings suggest that because the cryptography sits in transaction formats and consensus rules, replacing it requires hard forks, and decentralized networks have no way to force quick adoption, making migration "slow and fragmented," IOSCO said. Accounts and smart contracts still controlled by vulnerable keys could stay exposed after a network adds quantum-resistant options, and the path to quantum resistance for Bitcoin wallets remains uphill.

Industry observers note that wallet makers face their own trade-offs. SHRINCS, the leading candidate for a post-quantum Bitcoin signature scheme, offers "stateful" signatures that are about 10 times smaller but can expose funds to theft if keys are reused beyond a set signing budget, Trezor CTO Tomáš Sušánka has mentioned. Trezor is considering making the larger, safer stateless option the default, and hardware wallets will also need post-quantum cryptography for firmware and device authentication, he added.

The report distinguished "on-spend" attacks, in which an attacker races to exploit a public key revealed by a pending transaction, from "at-rest" attacks on keys left exposed for longer. Dormant or abandoned coins pose a particular problem where their holders can't move them. Crypto firms have formed a quantum alliance as some 6 million BTC sit in exposed addresses, and Bitcoin developer Cory Fields has proposed "quantum landmines" to make attacks on such coins costly.

According to recent reports, layer-2 networks are not insulated either. Optimistic rollups could face forged signatures during their dispute windows, typically seven days on Ethereum, and many zero-knowledge rollups use SNARK proofs that rely on elliptic curves. Hash-based STARK proofs are more resistant, but a rollup is only as safe as the layer-1 contracts, bridges and governance keys it depends on, the report mentioned.

Developers are already working on fixes. Researchers have proposed several ways to make Bitcoin quantum-safe, StarkWare has shown a quantum-safe Bitcoin transaction, and Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said the network is betting its future on quantum resistance.

In a recent development, IOSCO said firms should migrate to post-quantum cryptography and build "crypto-agility," the ability to update cryptographic systems without major redesign. Quantum key distribution could complement those measures on selected high-security channels, it added.

Most preparations across financial markets are still at an early stage, focused on awareness, governance, training and identifying vulnerable systems, according to the report, which drew on a March 2026 survey of members of IOSCO's Fintech Task Force and discussions with experts. Some respondents described "quantum-procrastination," in which firms put off action while waiting for clearer regulatory signals or wider adoption.

Recent findings suggest that no surveyed jurisdiction reported operational deployment of quantum computing in regulated financial services. The watchdog also urged regulators to act against "quantum washing," in which firms overstate the role, maturity or performance of quantum technology. IOSCO said it will treat quantum as a priority in 2027, focusing on raising awareness across the financial ecosystem.

According to recent reports, quantum hardware is advancing promptly. IBM has claimed a trusted quantum advantage, and Google has remarked it has cracked some of the field's biggest bottlenecks.

Industry observers note that bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report showed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses.

In a recent development, the selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low.

U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

In a recent development, leveraged traders took heavy losses as the bitcoin price broke support. Bitcoin liquidations hit $712.9 million over 24 hours, with $614 million coming from long positions. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to $18 billion from $20 billion a week ago, and funding rates flipped broadly negative as traders unwound their bets.

Traders are now watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the $60,000 area. A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022.

Institutional investors added 49,229 BTC through U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in the third quarter, lifting their holdings to a record 356,491 BTC. Industry observers note that bitcoin (BTC) fell as low as $55,081 on Nov. 21, its lowest price since September 2024, according to TradingView data. The cryptocurrency then bounced back and was trading at $60,583 on Sunday, after it opened November at $77,425.

According to recent reports, bitcoin has lost 21.6% so far in November 2026, according to CryptoRank. The last time Bitcoin had a worse month was June 2022, when the cryptocurrency lost 37.9%, according to the same data.

Recent findings suggest that the four-year cycle theory ties Bitcoin's market cycles to halvings, and its supporters point to 2014, 2018 and 2022 as the years when each bear market went through its final sell-off. In this context, 2026 is the next year in that row, and the next Bitcoin halving is expected in April 2028. The previous three halvings took place in July 2016, May 2020 and April 2024.

Bitcoin set its record above $1,100 in late 2013. In February 2014, the Japanese exchange Mt. Gox, which handled most Bitcoin trading in 2013, filed for bankruptcy after it lost about 850,000 BTC. In November 2014, Bitcoin gained 11.6%, according to CryptoRank, but December of that year brought a 15.3% drop, and the bottom below $200 came in January 2015.

In December 2017, Bitcoin reached a record near $20,000 on the back of the ICO boom, and during 2018, the ICO market dried up. In November 2018, the crypto market crashed after the Bitcoin Cash hard fork and the so-called hash war between the two camps of miners, and Bitcoin lost 36.4% that month. The cryptocurrency then lost another 6.4% in December 2018 and set its cycle low at about $3,200 in the middle of that month.

The 2021 record near $69,000 came in November 2021. In May 2022, the Terra ecosystem collapsed, and in July of that year, Celsius and Three Arrows Capital filed for bankruptcy. In November of that year, the FTX exchange went bankrupt. Bitcoin lost 16.1% in November 2022 and set its bear market bottom at around $15,500 on Nov. 21, 2022, four years to the day before the latest low. December of that year brought a 3.7% loss, and in January 2023, Bitcoin gained 39.9%.

Recent findings suggest that in the current cycle, Bitcoin set its record above $126,000 in October 2025. In 2026, Bitcoin has lost value in six of the 11 months so far, according to CryptoRank. On Nov. 20, the cryptocurrency fell below $60,000 for the first time since July, and the decline continued the next day.

The latest drop comes amid a broad sell-off on Wall Street, where technology and AI stocks came under pressure, and amid expectations of further interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

It has been revealed that A year ago, Zcash [ZEC] began a remarkable rally. After gently ticking upward from $34 to $60 in August and September 2025, the privacy token led an explosive sector-wide bullish charge.

It helped kick off a wave of bullish enthusiasm for ZEC as well as the privacy sector. Zcash surged by 1,135% in five weeks, Dash [DASH] rallied 605%, and Monero [XMR] was up by 181% from early October, though its move took longer, until January 2026.

Neither of the latter two tokens has managed to regain the highs they made back then.

Meanwhile, ZEC reached $1,700. The altcoin’s correction in recent months back below $1,000 has sparked bearish short-term sentiment, even though it was still trading above the previous year’s peak.

According to recent reports, apart from expansion on the price front, the privacy sector leaders have made substantial progress in 2026. The need for privacy is nuanced. Consumers want confidential smart contracts, not just standalone privacy.

In a recent development, presently, Monero uses RingCT to hide transactions. RingCT, along with CLSAG ring signatures, enforces a fixed ring size of 16- 15 decoys plus one real input. This makes it harder to trace the address for each transaction, without requiring other consumers to break deterministic trails, which privacy methods such as CoinJoin for Bitcoin require.

Sophisticated on-chain analysis can still narrow down to the 16 possibilities over multiple “hops”, or intermediate payments or asset transfers along a transaction trail.

It has been revealed that monero’s Full Chain Membership Proofs++ (FCMP++) eliminates the need for decoys. It replaces rings by providing zero-knowledge membership proofs across the entire blockchain output set. In other words, it mathematically proves that the spent XMR belongs to the Monero blockchain, making every previous output created part of the decoy set.

A mainnet activation date has not been confirmed for the FCMP++ and Carrot, the addressing protocol and wallet key hierarchy upgrade designed for the FCMP++ network upgrade. AMBCrypto reported that zkSecurity’s audit of FCMP++ was “complete, zero-knowledge, and sound”.

While Monero enforces privacy on every transaction, Zcash gives owners the option of privacy. It has transparent transactions, but also allows the use of zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) when shielded addresses are used.

Industry observers note that using zero-knowledge cryptography, private ZEC balances and transactions are tracked in shielded pools. Zcash has five of these shielded pools, as well as its transparent pool. Once funds are inside, the older pools can not be shut down, but can be made spend-only.

The Ironwood (NU6.3) upgrade was launched on the 28th of July, 2026, addressing the Orchard “infinity” bug found in May. It also introduced a latest shielded pool and restricted the Orchard pool. Funds exiting Orchard must now pass through Zcash’s turnstile, for supply integrity verification, to enter Ironwood.

The NU7 upgrade implemented in November aims to reduce block processing times by 67%, from 75 seconds to 25 seconds. It also reduced the wallet scanning workload required to perform private payments.

The upgrades are an encouraging sight for long-term users and investors. At the same time, the use case for privacy is also expanding.

When transactions are shielded in some form, anti-money laundering (AML) tracing is hindered or prevented. This brings strict regulatory restrictions on shielded transactions, as they require visibility in fund flows to prevent illicit financing.

As open blockchains, such as Ethereum [ETH] and Solana [SOL], enter the financial mainstream, institutional adoption requires them to address privacy. Their open nature means accessibility risks become a competitive liability and can have legal, financial, or operational repercussions.

Blockchain data and analytics platform Chainalysis wrote that institutional adoption is accelerating privacy network growth. Institutions must choose the right technology for their needs, whether it be shielded pools (like Zcash) or encrypted extensions (like Solana’s confidential transfers).

Canton [CC] is purpose-built for institutions. The network’s sub-transaction privacy hides all transaction details, even the transaction’s existence, from all but the parties involved. This segmented information sharing embeds privacy into the chain.

There is a case to be made for both financial privacy and financial oversight. The former argues for a fundamental right in a world of persistent data collection and financial surveillance.

The latter argues that oversight is a necessity to prevent serious crimes and to detect and disrupt illicit activity.

Elliptic, another blockchain analytics tech giant that provides crypto compliance software, noted that crypto projects can embed compliance-supporting features without wholly abandoning privacy.

Selective disclosure, such as in Zcash, Midnight, or using Identity Frameworks in Ethereum, can achieve this by sharing transaction details without revealing the entire financial history.

Zero-knowledge compliance is another approach that can prove that a transaction meets certain criteria, without exposing other relevant details.

Finding this middle ground between oversight and privacy is becoming increasingly notable to create a secure, yet private, digital future.

The primary federal regulator must grant a waiver, and its terms must cover the relevant Section 3 restriction. Relief can run for up to 12 months from the law’s effective date.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) has a separate final rule that requires a written request and a substantially complete issuer application pending on or before January 18, 2027. It can grant relief on public-interest grounds or in extraordinary circumstances. Its licensing page says it has yet to open applications or waiver requests and is awaiting clearance for its application forms.

The OCC waiver rule gives active issuers a route to request temporary relief before the January deadline.

It indicates qualifying issuers can keep issuing if their state’s rules are substantially similar and the state files within a year, until any final denial. The initial state filing is due within a year of the Act taking effect.

The issuer stated direct redemptions ended November 11 and that remaining balances are subject to mandatory redemption. ZUSD’s wind-down was already underway months before Treasury published its proposal.

Under the GENIUS Act, January 18, 2027 is the effective date for the U.S. issuance restriction. If a state-regulated issuer has to pause, the immediate effect would be on its ability to supply fresh units to customers and distributors. Trading already-issued tokens and redeeming them with the issuer are separate activities.

Sources indicate that starting July 18, 2028, digital asset service providers such as exchanges generally can offer or sell payment stablecoins to people in the U.S. only if the issuer is permitted or an exception applies.

A separate foreign-issuer provision applies from the Act’s effective date. It conditions U.S. platform availability on the foreign issuer’s ability and commitment to comply with lawful orders and reciprocal arrangements. Section 18 also provides a route for foreign issuers from comparable regimes that register with the OCC and meet other conditions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Famous Bitcoin (BTC) advocate and investor Bill Miller IV remarked that it is much easier to value the world's largest cryptocurrency than AI investments, even though Bitcoin does not produce any cash flow.

He said that this has to do with the expectations investors have when it comes to these two assets, specifically regarding their capacity to deliver future profits.

In a recent X post, Miller, who is the chairman and chief investment officer of Miller Value Partners, broke down why he thinks that it's easier to make an investment case for Bitcoin than for AI companies.

"Bitcoin and AI owners have different expectations. The owners of AI expect companies will one day produce free cash flow. Bitcoin owners never did or will expect this," Miller said.

And the end result is that "the valuation case is still much easier for Bitcoin than AI.".

Simply put, when investors buy stocks in AI companies, there is an expectation that at some point these companies will deliver big profits and free cash flow.

Free cash flow is the money a firm produces from its operations after capital expenditures. This is a significant metric for understanding the value of a company.

However, when it comes to AI companies, it can be difficult to assign a value because investors need to try to determine what kind of revenue these companies will generate, how much they will invest in infrastructure, and when these investments will start to deliver sufficient returns.

Miller has made it a point to push back against the argument that Bitcoin does not have value because it doesn't produce cash flow.

In a commentary from June 30, Miller explained that the traditional way of looking at intrinsic value, which revolves around future cash flows, doesn't really capture the potential of Bitcoin as a decentralized monetary network.

Instead, Miller stated that Bitcoin's value could be determined by comparing its potential role within the global financial system to that of gold.

Recent findings suggest that in his view, Bitcoin could theoretically reach about $1.4 million per coin if it achieved a valuation similar to gold's. At least, that's what he calculated at the time.

  • According to recent reports, the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday.

According to recent reports, the price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater.

The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price.

Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market.

Recent findings suggest that the MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost.

In a recent development, the firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report.

Industry observers note that “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.”.

Industry observers note that the slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day.

The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week.

Recent findings suggest that leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total.

CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18.

The note frames Friday’s price action as a late stage of a decline that began well before November. Butterfill pointed to whale selling that weighed on prices from late 2025, expectations of higher interest rates and weakness in technology stocks, all of which have kept buyers cautious.

According to recent reports, “Our base case remains range trading around USD 60k to 90k through much of 2027, until falling inflation gives monetary policy room to ease,” he stated. “Geopolitics will have a considerable say in that.”.

In a recent development, A move through the realized price would put bitcoin near the bottom edge of that range. The firm said holders as a group have not been in loss since early 2023.

A sustained breakout, Butterfill noted, would likely require “a change in the policy outlook, renewed whale participation or both.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that crypto exchanges spent the past week rolling out tokenized U.S stocks to buyers around the world. On an unrelated note, Nvidia slid by 30% from its ATH in a month following Jensen Huang’s departure. All while AMD rose — an early sign of decoupling.

Sources indicate that one story is about tokenization, while the other is about AI stocks. However, both skirt around the same topic: a growing class of investors being handed exposure they don’t fully understand by markets that do not care to explain it.

For most people outside the U.S, buying an Apple or Nvidia stock is hard. It is either expensive, tedious, or simply unavailable. Pritam Dutta, Founder and CEO of Zoth, explained the same when he spoke to AMBCrypto, stating,.

There’s a lot of excitement around tokenized stocks right now. Most people outside the U.S. still can’t easily buy shares in Apple, Nvidia and the rest of the Magnificent Seven. Tokenization changes that.

Sources indicate that undoubtedly, for a buyer in Nigeria or the Philippines, a tokenized stock could be their first realistic route into U.S markets. But Dutta’s next point is the one that should make an investor sit up and take notice.

In a recent development, A lot of what’s launching gives you price exposure, not the share itself. You don’t get voting rights, and dividends depend on the platform’s terms… Too few platforms are being upfront about it.

Recent findings suggest that in a nutshell, investors are not buying Apple. They are buying a token that tracks Apple’s price, issued by a platform whose terms determine what else you get, subject to its discretion.

Dutta, then, reduced the entire conversation to three questions investors must ask themselves before running towards such stocks.

In a recent development, who holds the real share? What happens to my dividends? What happens if the platform fails?

These are not clever questions. These are the questions you should ask before buying anything that is marketed as “tokenized.” Unfortunately, the fact that they need to be asked in the first place is a sure-shot sign of how little the platforms are disclosing.

In today’s age, the access is real, but the understanding might not be. And, that gap is the hardest on buyers with the least room to make an error.

Industry observers note that nvidia fell this week while AMD rose. The easy explanation is Jensen Huang’s exit. However, Ian Weisberger, CEO of CoinRoutes, believes that there is a larger cause. He told AMBCrypto,.

The real problem is that Nvidia’s chips are becoming a commodity.

Recent findings suggest that for years, Nvidia and the AI boom were not seen as two separate entities, simply because of the former’s chips. That is also how the manufacturer grew to roughly 8% of the S&P 500.

This week, though the market began pulling the two apart — and within the AI sector — the separation was underway long before anyone realized.

In a recent development, anyone who has built on both stacks knows the gap is closing. As the chips become interchangeable, buyers will shop on price, and the profits will move to the companies building products on top of them.

That is the concentration problem in one paragraph. When a single stock is 8% of the AI sector, millions of retail investors own a large position in it through their index funds. That is exposure they never signed up to be a part of.

The AI boom is not ending, but the era of one stock carrying the index might be.

According to recent reports, both stories have the same problem — the people most likely to be hurt are unfortunately the least equipped to protect themselves. Here’s why.

Firstly, tokenized stocks are best for an overseas buyer for whom a U.S brokerage account is out of reach. Unfortunately, that buyer is also the first to suffer losses if their platform of choice fails.

Secondly, when it comes to artificial intelligence, the cracks are less noticeable. Most overseas retail investors own Nvidia through an index fund that was marketed to them as “diversified.” This causes the investor with the least information to hold one of the most important market bets.

As Nicolai Sondergaard, research analyst at Nansen, told AMBCrypto:.

AI and crypto draw on the same pool of risk capital, so when Nvidia sells off, the money goes to cash, not into Bitcoin.

In a recent development, at the time of Sondergaard’s analysis, Nvidia was down about 32% from its 6th October high, Bitcoin [BTC] was 26% below its September peak, and gold was 17% off its August high. Meanwhile, the dollar was at a six-month high, and real yields were up more than 0.2 percentage points in two months.

So, the investor who thought they were spread across AI and crypto was actually holding double the risk. And in the worst case, they must have not figured it out before it was too late.

The same story can be crafted across different markets — the sophisticated investor can take on the risk, while the overseas investor cannot. Regardless, the product holds no difference when marketing to them.

The demand is real. The question is whether people are being sold what they think they’re buying.

The question at the end of it all is — were buyers sold a dream that was impossible to achieve? Looking further, was the promised portfolio diversification ever there at all?

Industry observers note that in the end, the retail investor’s blind spot is not ignorance. It is the industry that keeps expanding faster than investors understand what’s going on, causing them to buy the narrative and allure. Not the reality.

Rethinking crypto risk — Here’s why ONE factor doesn’t tell the whole story

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (752 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ambcrypto

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Investors have a habit of gauging crypto by a single risk framework.
  • According to recent reports, bitcoin’s [BTC] daily price fluctuations are about three times wider than the S&P 500’s, with far more extreme moves in both directions.
  • So, investors should be aware of three things — where returns come from, how they fit inside a portfolio, and how crypto has grown far beyond Bitcoin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investors have a habit of gauging crypto by a single risk framework. However, currently, that framework no longer captures how the market works.

According to recent reports, bitcoin’s [BTC] daily price fluctuations are about three times wider than the S&P 500’s, with far more extreme moves in both directions. However, the realized volatility of Bitcoin has declined over time to the level of individual large-cap U.S stocks.

So, investors should be aware of three things — where returns come from, how they fit inside a portfolio, and how crypto has grown far beyond Bitcoin.

The standard risk tools like the standard deviation or the Sharpe ratio don’t care how much money you make or lose. That leaves a blind spot for Bitcoin as most of its long-term gains come from just a handful of trading days.

Sources indicate that bitcoin has averaged 60% per year over the last three years. If you take away its ten best days, that number drops to 7%. If you take away its ten worst days, the number jumps to 197%. That’s because big drops are often followed by big rebounds, so investors who try to avoid bad days can easily miss the best ones.

According to recent reports, momentum counts as well. Bitcoin’s gains tend to pile on top of each other, and Bitcoin runs far better after months of winning than months of losing. During strong rallies, the Sortino ratio can rise well above normal risk scores. Mostly because it only measures returns against downside volatility, not upside volatility.

According to recent reports, notably, Bitcoin has dropped by 50% or more seven times since 2011. But when you include the volatility of starting, Bitcoin’s falls look more like stocks and bonds.

In fact, even “low risk” bonds have been falling for a while in recent years.

While massive price moves can be alarming on their own, portfolio managers care most about how an asset behaves when put together with the other assets they own. Changes in stocks, bonds, and the private market are mostly driven by common economic factors. However, these factors explain the changes in Bitcoin much less.

Cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, have historically shown low correlation with traditional measures than with each other. This is the case, even though correlations can increase during periods of market stress.

Large organizations have taken this into account too. For instance, J.P. Morgan Asset Management, an organization with $5 trillion in assets, introduced Bitcoin into its 2027 outlook, estimating a 10% per year return in the coming ten years. This correlates by only 33% with major U.S. equities, even less than international equities, corporate bonds, and hedge funds, even when there is 55% volatility.

Industry observers note that this provides a unique combination of both high expected returns and little correlation with core equities. History proves that including a small portion of Bitcoin in an average institutional portfolio can increase returns and efficiency without increasing overall risk or maximum losses.

Notably, Mike Belshe, CEO of BitGo, recently pointed out JPMorgan’s changing perspective on crypto. He stated,.

Let that sink in. The world’s largest bank, long crypto-skeptical, is now publicly supporting crypto market structure legislation. This is a different ballgame.

Another mistake is treating crypto as a single Bitcoin bet. The modern landscape of crypto includes smart contract platforms, decentralized finance, consumer applications, and artificial intelligence. Each having its own unique users and economics.

Over the last three years, Bitcoin has accounted for just about 50% of volatility in returns on all major crypto sectors, while correlations among sectors have decreased.

Out of the top 10 biggest non-stablecoin crypto assets by market cap, six different tokens have been leading returns on a quarter-by-quarter basis over the last two years. Bitcoin has never led once.

None of this implies that crypto is risk-free though. Especially since a rally could unwind swiftly. On the contrary, risk is not something that can be boiled down to one simple figure.

A uniform know-how about crypto implies understanding of multiple factors — volatility of the asset, distribution of returns, correlation with the rest of a portfolio, and the performance of various sectors separately.

Therefore, in reality, instead of trying to overlook any price fluctuations, it is crucial to view them with a proper perspective.

Rather than discussing the volatility of crypto per se, one should think of what kind of risks it introduces, what risks from one’s portfolio it offsets, and what additional sources of profit appear outside of Bitcoin.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that AI systems tasked with building business agents often gave their work near-perfect grades on tests they wrote themselves. In a Nov. 19 preprint, researchers at Uniphore found that the grades could improve far more than scores on cases withheld from the builders during development.

Sources indicate that the researchers used AppSci-Bench, a benchmark that puts AI builders to work in seven simulated business workflows, including invoice review, customer relationship management and airline rebooking. A builder could ask a simulated business user what the agent needed to do, then develop it using the tools and data available in that setting.

In the test runs that allowed revisions, builders could write their own tests and keep changes that raised the score. After the builder submitted an agent, the benchmark ran it on separate cases withheld during development. The researchers released the benchmark code and recorded results alongside the preprint.

Uniphore researchers found that 86 of the 132 builds with a recorded self-test scored at least 99% on the tests their builders wrote. The researchers tracked 13 Claude Opus 4.8 builds that could revise their agents, comparing the first round of testing with the last. For those builds, scores rose an average of 16.9 points on tests the model wrote and 3.2 points on the withheld cases. In six of the 24 revision steps the researchers examined in that subset, the builder's grade rose while the withheld-case score held steady.

Sources indicate that AI builders could use their own tests to decide which changes to keep. AppSci-Bench also tested the submitted agents on cases withheld during development.

A large gain on the builder’s tests can coexist with a much smaller gain on unseen cases.

In a recent development, the evaluations used different cases and scoring rules. AppSci-Bench tested simulated business workflows.

It has been revealed that the bars use the same zero-to-20 point scale. Both values are mean changes per build from first to final checkpoint in Table 3 of the Uniphore preprint.

The evaluations used different cases and scoring rules. AppSci-Bench tested simulated business workflows.

Sources indicate that in a broader comparison of 252 builds using Claude Opus 5, Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5, the researchers found no statistically significant difference in withheld-case scores when they switched the test-and-revise loop on or off. That result held in both the researchers’ setup and the models’ native coding tools, Claude Code and Codex, after accounting for multiple comparisons.

One banking build showed how a test could reinforce a bad assumption. GPT-5.5 assumed it could not look customers up by email or name even though both options were available. One test it wrote rewarded asking for a customer ID, and the agent ended up refusing the other lookups. The agent eventually scored a perfect 1.0 on its builder’s tests. In the withheld trial the researchers examined, it succeeded on five of 97 cases.

Meta used a live search test after its AI agents screened candidate changes offline.

According to recent reports, for a team evaluating a banking agent, a test that supplies only an email address could expose the same blind spot. Keeping a set of cases outside development lets the team see how the submitted agent handles situations its builder’s tests may never have covered.

Block Notes Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
